Cite this lesson Video Summary for Revenue in Accounting Revenue in accounting refers to income earned from the sale of goods or services. This video explains the distinction between gross revenue (before subtracting costs) and net revenue (income remaining after expenses). Revenue appears on income statements but isn't equivalent to profit, as costs might exceed income earned. While all revenue is income, not all income comes from revenue. Income sources include: Sales revenue Wages and salaries Investment income Interest income Profits from asset sales The video demonstrates these concepts through a practical example of an accountant preparing a quarterly income statement, showing how different revenue and income sources contribute to a company's financial position.
